name: Vansen ChemShell Acid-Rated Coverall Pro
description: Vansen's ChemShell is a Circuit-tier staple — a single-piece coverall in flat industrial yellow with black chemical-resistance rating stripes across the chest and thighs. The outer shell is thermoplastic-bonded polyaramid, stiff at the shoulders but articulated at the elbows and knees with accordion gussets. Seams are triple-welded and color-coded by rating class. A chest pocket holds a folded decon wipe sleeve. The hood is detachable via quarter-turn collar locks. Finish is matte and scuffs to a worn sheen after a few shifts.
functionality: Rated for concentrated sulfuric, hydrochloric, and nitric acid splash exposure. Integrated nitrile wrist seals mate with compatible gauntlets. Decon-ready surface — low chemical absorption, wipe-clean exterior. Hood locks provide airtight collar seal when paired with a full-face respirator.
what_it_says: You follow the safety protocols because you've seen what happens when someone doesn't.
story_hooks: A Vansen ChemShell with a forged rating stripe — upgraded from Class B to Class A on paper — has been circulating in Circuit markets; the forgery is nearly undetectable.
The quarter-turn collar lock is also used as an improvised restraint mechanism by at least one known Shelf enforcer.
A worker survived a full chemical bath in this suit when a pipe burst — the suit was rated for splash, not immersion. It held anyway. Barely.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian full-body coverall with high-visibility industrial yellow as the dominant color, broken by bold black chemical-resistance rating stripes across the chest and thighs. The silhouette is practical and blocky—shoulders sit squared-off, arms hang straight, legs are wide through the thigh. The detachable hood adds a technical, modular appearance when attached. Overall impression: no-nonsense safety worker, unglamorous but purpose-built.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and intentionally loose through the torso and limbs to allow layering and movement in hazardous environments. Accordion gussets at elbows and knees provide articulation without restricting motion. The shoulders are stiff and structured, tapering slightly at wrists and ankles where elastic cuffs grip. Designed for function over form.
physical_description.primary_material: Thermoplastic-bonded polyaramid—a synthetic composite rated for acid and chemical exposure. The outer shell is rigid and shell-like, with a matte industrial finish that gradually burnishes to a worn sheen with use.
physical_description.texture: Matte, slightly rough to the touch with a plasticky, reinforced quality. Accordion gussets at joints have a ribbed, folded appearance. Triple-welded seams create subtle ridges. Scuffs and micro-abrasions develop naturally with wear, adding tactile variety to the finish.
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat industrial yellow (Φ-grade safety standard) with crisp black chemical-resistance rating stripes running horizontally across chest and thighs. No fading intended; any weathering is from physical damage, not dye degradation. Color-coded seams (likely red, orange, green, blue) by hazard class.
physical_description.closures: Front-center heavy-duty zipper running full length from crotch to chin. Quarter-turn collar locks secure the detachable hood. Elastic cuffs at wrists and ankles. No additional buckles or snaps—all closures are functional and sealed.
distinctive_features: Detachable, modular hood with quarter-turn locking mechanism
Triple-welded seams with color-coded rating stripes (hazard classification system)
Accordion gussets at elbows and knees for articulation
Integrated chest pocket with folded decon wipe sleeve storage
Thermoplastic-bonded shell resistant to acid, caustics, and industrial solvents
Matte finish that scuffs and wears to a reflective sheen
Wide, loose cut designed for hazmat responders and chemical plant workers
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 working class. This is standard-issue safety wear for Circuit-tier industrial workers, chemical handlers, and hazmat responders. Affordable, durable, and regulation-compliant—not luxury, but not salvage either.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this signals honest industrial labor, chemical exposure risk tolerance, and regulatory compliance. The wearer is likely a plant worker, hazmat specialist, or decon technician in the GLMZ manufacturing sectors. It's not street wear; it's visible proof of a dangerous job.
physical_description.condition_typical: New: stiff, bright yellow, pristine matte finish. Worn (1-3 shifts): micro-scuffing visible, elastic cuffs slightly relaxed. Heavy use (1+ month): visible scratches on the yellow shell, seams show wear patterns, hood may be detached and clipped to the belt. Industrial wear is expected and not considered damage.
